newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Three Swedish parties agree to close nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Three Swedish parties agree to close nuclear plant.

text.p: Three Swedish political parties agreed to close both nuclear reactors at the Barseback power station in 1998, Swedish radio said on Monday.
The Social Democrats, the Centre Party and the Left Party agreed to close one reactor before the general election in 1998 and the other one after.
Negotiations will begin with Barseback's owner, Swedish power company Sydkraft AB, about replacing the power source with either natural gas or oil, the radio said.
The decision come after 17 years of disagreement since a national referendum in 1980 when Swedes voted to gradually phase out nuclear power.
Parliament eventually set 2010 as the target for making Sweden nuclear-free, but critics of the plan say Sweden has not made alternative arrangements for electricity supply.
Barseback, located at the southern tip of Sweden, is visible from neighbouring Denmark.
